keyFindings.description: Security[transport]: declarationParser.Parse (line 59) walks to the block's end from every `<!` and letter with no `>`, and keeps nothing between tries, so parsing is quadratic. Measured by the reviewer: Parse of `p ` + `<!a` repeated to 1 MiB takes 9.9 s at the head against 0.22 s at the fork point 08c2e8ad; ParseForWrite accepts that 1 MiB write after 18.9 s; `<!A` doubles (10.0 s to 19.5 s for Parse, 48.9 s for ParseForWrite) because goldmark's raw HTML parser at 400 repeats the same walk after this one fails. The deep review measured the multi-line form (`x <!a` per line) at 9.6 s for 64 KiB and about 4x per doubling (≈7 min of one core per 1 MiB write). Fix: remember in parser.Context where no `>` remains in the block, as rawHTMLScan.ends already does on the writer side; read every declaration with one parser (wrap goldmark's raw HTML parser in place at 400, as declarationBlockParser wraps the block parser) so `<!A` is not scanned twice; add single-line and multi-line `<!a` and `<!A` shapes to linear_test.go. The pre-existing goldmark walks for `<!--`, `<?` and CDATA (linear_test.go:306-307) are reported to the INFRA-138 architect.
